findings.evidence:
`pkg/infoschema/infoschema_v2.go:1002` switches full bundle rebuild to scan `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute(PlacementPolicyAttribute)` instead of all schemas/tables.
Placement-policy tables are now inserted into `Data.tableInfoResident` because `hasSpecialAttributes` includes `PlacementPolicyAttribute` (`pkg/infoschema/infoschema_v2.go:187`, `pkg/infoschema/infoschema_v2.go:1074`).
`tableInfoResident` is ordered by `dbName` first (`pkg/infoschema/infoschema_v2.go:263`). The listing logic iterates in reverse and “dedups” only consecutive same `tableID` *before* tomb handling (`pkg/infoschema/infoschema_v2.go:1081`).
Cross-database `RENAME TABLE` keeps the same `TableID` (`pkg/ddl/ddl_api.go:7203`), and v2 diff application writes a tomb record into `tableInfoResident` using the *old* dbName (`pkg/infoschema/builder.go:370`, `pkg/infoschema/infoschema_v2.go:934`, `pkg/infoschema/infoschema_v2.go:216`).
If the old-db tomb item and new-db live item become adjacent in the reverse iteration order (e.g., minimal setup with only the moved table as the only “resident” entry in each DB), `lastTableID` can cause the live record to be skipped, so the tableID never reaches `updateTableBundles` and its bundle is missing. Full reload reuses existing `do.infoCache.Data` (`pkg/domain/domain.go:317`), so the tomb/live combination can persist into the full-rebuild path.
findings.fix: Make `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute` choose the latest non-tomb record per `tableID` by comparing `schemaVersion` across *all* dbNames (e.g., collect best-per-tableID in a map, then group by dbName), or change `tableInfoResident` ordering/indexing to be `tableID`-first for correct dedup and group results afterward. Avoid relying on dbName-ordered iteration + `lastTableID` for correctness when dbName can change across versions.
findings.impact: On a full infoschema v2 reload (deltaUpdate=false), `ruleBundleMap` may miss placement bundles for affected tables/partitions. This breaks placement-policy/txn-scope semantics: `PlacementBundleByPhysicalTableID` returns false, causing local-txn commit checks to error (`pkg/session/session.go:4040`) or txn-scope verification to behave incorrectly (`pkg/distsql/request_builder.go:702`). The failure can persist until another bundle rebuild/update happens.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09`: `updateInfoSchemaBundlesV2` still rebuilds bundles from `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute(PlacementPolicyAttribute)`, and the v2 resident list still uses dbName-first ordering with lastTableID-based dedup (no evident fix for cross-db rename adjacency).
findings.verify: Add a regression test that: (1) creates two DBs where old DB name sorts after new DB name, (2) creates a table with placement policy in old DB, (3) `RENAME TABLE oldDB.t TO newDB.t`, (4) forces a full infoschema v2 rebuild (deltaUpdate=false / full load path), then asserts `PlacementBundleByPhysicalTableID(tableID)` is present and `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute(PlacementPolicyAttribute)` returns the table under the new DB.
findings.what: Full placement-bundle rebuild in infoschema v2 can miss some placement-policy tables after cross-database `RENAME TABLE`, due to `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute` iterating `tableInfoResident` ordered by dbName and deduping only consecutive `tableID`s (with tomb handling after dedup). In certain key-order adjacency cases, the old-db tomb record can cause the new-db live record to be skipped, leaving `ruleBundleMap` incomplete.

subject: infoschema: make build bundle faster for infoschema v2 (#53821)
summary: Change speeds up infoschema v2 placement bundle rebuild by using the resident “special tables” index and a new `PlacementPolicyAttribute` filter. However, the new full-rebuild path now depends on `ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute`’s dbName-ordered scan + `lastTableID` dedup, which can skip a placement-policy table after cross-database renames in certain iteration-adjacency cases, producing missing placement bundles on full reload; this pattern is still present on upstream/master.
